clinician.final_diagnosis: c-ANCA positive IBD with prominent extraintestinal manifestations preceding GI complaints.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old man presented with a history of recurrent inflammatory extraintestinal manifestations, including anterior uveitis, auricular chondritis, and right wrist synovitis (E001). Initially, he had an episode of fever and diarrhea suspected to be viral, which resolved. However, 8 weeks later, he developed severe gastrointestinal symptoms including hematochezia, left lower quadrant pain, and a perirectal abscess and fistula (E005). Subsequent workup included colonoscopy with biopsies showing cryptitis, crypt abscesses, early crypt distortion, and basal plasmacytosis, suggestive of chronic colitis and/or IBD (E006). Serology revealed positive c-ANCA with elevated proteinase 3 (E003). Based on these findings, treatment for IBD was initiated with azathioprine and infliximab, leading to healing of his fistula and sustained clinical improvement without further GI or extraintestinal manifestations for 1.5 years (E007).

Patient tested positive for c-ANCA with elevated proteinase 3.
